# Helical phase as a positioning coordinate

## Historical hypothesis

Linear spacer length can hide a rotational variable: two constructs with similar distance can present the catalytic domain toward different faces of the DNA-bound scaffold.

## Why it was interesting

The idea changes the causal coordinate from linker length to azimuthal presentation. It predicts periodic rather than monotonic changes across a geometry series.

## Why it was archived

The historical evidence supported structural plausibility, not a complete mitochondrial TALED implementation. There was no sequence-level demonstration that an azimuthal shift narrowed the A-to-G window while preserving useful target activity.

## Decisive pattern

Support would require a periodic window shift across matched geometry variants that cannot be explained by global activity collapse.

## Kill criterion

Archive permanently if geometry changes only total activity or if window effects do not reproduce across loci.
